newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola nearbys end up on Japan rumors.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola nearbys end up on Japan rumors.

text.p: WCE nearby canola ended up on rumours of large Japan export demand, traders said.

"We're up on talk Japan bought 20,000 tonnes overnight and that they're short for December canola deliveries," a trader said. Japanese demand for canola was weaker in November than in October, sources said.
Deferred futures fell as commercial elevators sold futures while farmers sold their 90-day storage certificates.

About 1,000 Jan-Mar spread at $0.80 and $1.00, May-July spread at $1.50. January futures crush profit margin fell to -41.74 from -38.75 Monday on January soyoil, meal. Futures volume was heavy at 5,500 lots, or 110,000 tonnes, with 225 hedges, traders said.
January canola rose $0.70 to $402.80, May fell $0.40 to $400.90. January flax lost $1 to $360, September fell $6.50 to $350.50 on commercial selling.
"September flax is weighing on the whole complex to keep spreads in line," a flax trader said.
December feed wheat fell $1.90 to $166.10 on closing hedges met by commercial buying, March fell $1.30 to $167.70. Dec-Mar at $1.50, Dec-May $1, Mar-May $0.50. Volume 1,075.
February western barley was unchanged at $138.50 on commercial short covering while feed lot buying limited March losses to down $0.10 at $137.90. Volume was 650 lots.
UGG bought December peas unchanged at US$203.50, Royal Bank of Canada Dominion Securities bought February unchanged at US$205, traders said. Volume was 110. Oats did not trade.
(All values in Canadian dollars per tonne except peas, oats).
